text: When a hydrocarbon A undergoes complete combustion it requires 11 equivalents of oxygen and produces 4 equivalents of water. What is the molecular formula of $A$ ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon $\mathrm{C}_{x}\mathrm{H}_{y}$:

$\mathrm{C}_{x}\mathrm{H}_{y}+\left (x+\dfrac{y}{4}\right )\mathrm{O}{}_{2}\to x\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}+\dfrac{y}{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Moles of water formed: $\dfrac{y}{2}=4\Rightarrow y=8$.

Moles of oxygen required: $x+\dfrac{8}{4}=11\Rightarrow x=9$.

So A is $\mathrm{C}{}_{9}\mathrm{H}{}_{8}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: Compound $\mathrm{A},\mathrm{C}_{5}\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_{5}$, gives a tetraacetate with $\mathrm{Ac}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and oxidation of $\mathrm{A}$ with $\mathrm{Br}_{2}-\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ gives an acid, $\mathrm{C}_{5}\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_{6}$. Reduction of $\mathrm{A}$ with $\mathrm{HI}$ gives isopentane. The possible structure of $\mathrm{A}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{C}{}_{5}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$ has one degree of unsaturation.

A tetraacetate with $\mathrm{Ac}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ shows four OH groups in A.

Bromine water oxidises A to $\mathrm{C}{}_{5}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}\mathrm{O}{}_{6}$ (one O added), which shows a CHO group oxidised to COOH; the one unsaturation is this CHO group.

HI removes all the oxygen and gives isopentane, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, so the five carbons form a branched chain.


[IMG]

Only option (B), $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}){}_{2}$, has four OH groups, a CHO group and a branched $\mathrm{C}{}_{5}$ skeleton; the straight-chain aldopentose (C) would give n-pentane.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Evaluate the following statements for their correctness.

A. The elevation in boiling point temperature of water will be same for $0.1\mathrm{M}\mathrm{NaCl}$ and $0.1\mathrm{M}$ urea.

B. Azeotropic mixtures boil without change in their composition.

C. Osmosis always takes place from hypertonic to hypotonic solution.

D. The density of $32%\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ solution having molarity $4.09\mathrm{M}$ is approximately $1.26\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mL}^{-1}$

E. A negatively charged sol is obtained when KI solution is added to silver nitrate solution.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) Elevation in boiling point temperature of water will
be higher for 0.1 M NaCl as compared to 0.1 M
urea.

(B) Azeotropic mixtures boil without change in their
composition

(C) Osmosis always takes place from hypotonic (low
concentration of solute) solution to hypertonic
(high concentration of solute) solution.

(E) When KI solution is added to AgNO$_{3}$ solution,  positively charged solution is formed due to adsorption of $Ag^{+}$ ions from dispersion medium.  

AgI$/ Ag^{+} ($positively charged) 

(D) Let the mass of $H_{2}SO_{4} (32$%) is 100.

$\therefore \text{Weight of}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}=32$

Moles of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}=\frac{32}{98}$

Now, $4.09=\frac{32}{98\times \mathrm{V}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=79\mathrm{ml}$

Density $=\frac{100}{79}=1.265$

Hence, correct answer is (C) B and D only.

text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R)

Assertion (A): The first ionization enthalpy of $3\mathrm{d}$ series elements is more than that of group 2 metals

Reason (R): In 3d series of elements successive filling of d-orbitals takes place.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but $(𝐑)$ is not the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First ionization enthalpies (kJ mol$^{−1})$:

  
    3d seriesScTiVCrMnFeCoNiCuZn
  
  
    IE631656650653717762758736745906
  

  
    Group 2BeMgCaSrBaRa
  
  
    IE899737590549503509
  

Assertion (A): Every 3d element (631 to 906) has a higher first ionization enthalpy than calcium (590), the group 2 metal of the same period (4th), and than the heavier group 2 metals Sr, Ba and Ra. So (A) is true.

Reason (R): Across the 3d series the added electrons go successively into the inner $3d$ orbitals, which shield the outer $4s$ electrons poorly. The effective nuclear charge felt by the $4s$ electrons therefore increases, which is why these elements have higher ionization enthalpies than Ca. So (R) is true and is the correct explanation of (A).

Hence option A, which is the official NTA answer. (Be and Mg, from earlier periods, have higher values than some 3d elements; the assertion compares elements of the same period.)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: A hydrocarbon ' $\mathrm{X}$ ' with formula $\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{8}$ uses two moles of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ on catalytic hydrogenation of its one mole. On ozonolysis, ' $\mathrm{X}$ ' yields two moles of methane dicarbaldehyde. The hydrocarbon ' $\mathrm{X}$ ' is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{8}$ has $\dfrac{2(6)+2-8}{2}=3$ degrees of unsaturation. Uptake of 2 mol $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ per mole shows two C=C bonds, so the third unsaturation is a ring.

Methane dicarbaldehyde is $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CHO}$. Two such $\mathrm{C}_{3}$ units from a six-membered ring require each C=C to be separated from the other by one $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ on each side, which is cyclohexa-1,4-diene:


[IMG]

Cyclohexa-1,3-diene gives $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CHO}$ and $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CHO}$ instead, and hexa-1,3,5-triene takes up 3 mol $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I: Upon heating a borax bead dipped in cupric sulphate in a luminous flame, the colour of the bead becomes green

Statement II: The green colour observed is due to the formation of copper(I) metaborate

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the borax bead test, a bead dipped in a copper(II) salt and heated in the oxidising (non-luminous) flame forms copper(II) metaborate, which gives the blue-green colour:

$\mathrm{CuSO}{}_{4}+\mathrm{B}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{BO}{}_{2}){}_{2}+\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}$

In the reducing (luminous) flame, copper(II) metaborate is reduced either to colourless copper(I) metaborate or to metallic copper, which makes the bead red and opaque:

$2~\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{BO}{}_{2}){}_{2}+2\mathrm{NaBO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{C}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{CuBO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{4}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}+\mathrm{CO}$

$2~\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{BO}{}_{2}){}_{2}+4\mathrm{NaBO}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{C}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Cu}+2\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{B}{}_{4}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}+2\mathrm{CO}$

So the bead does not become green in the luminous flame, and Statement I is false.

Copper(I) metaborate is colourless; the green colour comes from copper(II) metaborate formed in the oxidising flame, so Statement II is also false.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: The incorrect statement for the use of indicators in acid-base titration is :
options: Phenolphthalein is a suitable indicator for a weak acid vs strong base titration.
Methyl orange may be used for a weak acid vs weak base titration.
Methyl orange is a suitable indicator for a strong acid vs weak base titration.
Phenolphthalein may be used for a strong acid vs strong base titration.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An indicator suits a titration when its colour-change range lies inside the steep pH jump at the equivalence point. Methyl orange changes colour at pH 3.1–4.4 and phenolphthalein at pH 8.3–10.

(A) Weak acid vs strong base: the equivalence point is basic and the jump lies at about pH 7–11, covering the range of phenolphthalein. The statement is correct.

(B) Weak acid vs weak base: the pH changes only gradually near the equivalence point, with no sharp jump, so no indicator, methyl orange included, gives a sharp end point. The statement is incorrect.

(C) Strong acid vs weak base: the equivalence point is acidic and the jump lies at about pH 3–7, covering the range of methyl orange. The statement is correct.

(D) Strong acid vs strong base: the jump spans about pH 3–11 around the equivalence point (pH 7), so both phenolphthalein and methyl orange change colour within it. The statement is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
Amongst the following, the number of species having the linear shape is $_________$.

$\mathrm{XeF}_{2},\mathrm{I}_{3}^{+},\mathrm{C}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{2},\mathrm{I}_{3}^{-},\mathrm{CO}_{2},\mathrm{SO}_{2},\mathrm{BeCl}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{BCl}_{2}^{⊖}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{XeF}{}_{2}$: Xe has 2 bp + 3 lp; the three lone pairs occupy the equatorial positions of a trigonal bipyramid, so the molecule is linear.


[IMG]

$\mathrm{C}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ ($\mathrm{O}=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$), $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ ($\mathrm{O}=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$) and monomeric $\mathrm{BeCl}{}_{2}$ ($\mathrm{Cl}-\mathrm{Be}-\mathrm{Cl}$) have sp-hybridised central atoms with no lone pair, so all three are linear.


[IMG]

$\mathrm{I}{}_{3}{}^{-}$: the central I has 7 + 1 = 8 valence electrons, 2 bp + 3 lp, so like $\mathrm{XeF}{}_{2}$ it is linear.


[IMG]

$\mathrm{I}{}_{3}{}^{+}$: the central I has 7 − 1 = 6 valence electrons, 2 bp + 2 lp, so it is bent.

$\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}$: S has 2 σ bonds + 1 lp ($sp^{2}$), so it is bent.

$\mathrm{BCl}{}_{2}{}^{-}$: B has 3 + 1 = 4 valence electrons, 2 bp + 1 lp ($sp^{2}$), so it is bent.

The linear species are $\mathrm{XeF}{}_{2}$, $\mathrm{C}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$, $\mathrm{I}{}_{3}{}^{-}$, $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{BeCl}{}_{2}$, 5 in all.

Hence, the answer is 5.

text:
Enthalpies of formation of $\mathrm{CCl}_{4}(\mathrm{g}),\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g}),\mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ and $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})$ are $-105,-242,-394$ and $-92\mathrm{kJ}$ $\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The magnitude of enthalpy of the reaction given below is $_________$ $\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (nearest integer)

$\mathrm{CCl}_{4}(\mathrm{g})+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+4\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{CCl}_{4}(\mathrm{g})+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+4\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})$

Enthalpy of above reaction

$\begin{array}{l} =\Delta \mathrm{H}_{f}(\mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{g}))+4\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{f}}(\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g}))-\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{f}}(\mathrm{CCl}_{4})-2\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{f}}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}) \\  \\ =-394-4\times 92+105+2\times 242 \\  \\ =-394-368+105+484 \\  \\ =-173\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \end{array}$

Hence the magnitude of this will be $173\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
If the CFSE of $[\mathrm{Ti}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}$ is $-96.0\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mol}$, this complex will absorb maximum at wavelength $___________$ $\mathrm{nm}$. (nearest integer)

Assume Planck's constant (h) $=6.4\times 10^{-34}\mathrm{Js}$, Speed of light $(\mathrm{c})=3.0\times 10^{8}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and Avogadro's

Constant $(\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}})=6\times 10^{23}/\mathrm{mol}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Ti}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{1}$ ($t_{2g}^{1}e_{g}^{0}$), so its CFSE is $-0.4\Delta _{o}$.

$-0.4\Delta _{o}=-96.0\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\Rightarrow \Delta _{o}=240\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Energy absorbed per ion:

$E=\dfrac{240\times 10^{3}\text{J mol}^{-1}}{6\times 10^{23}\text{mol}^{-1}}=4.0\times 10^{-19}\text{J}$

$λ=\dfrac{hc}{E}=\dfrac{6.4\times 10^{-34}\times 3.0\times 10^{8}}{4.0\times 10^{-19}}=4.8\times 10^{-7}\text{m}=480\text{nm}$

Hence, the answer is 480.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
The rate constant for a first order reaction is $20\min ^{-1}$. The time required for the initial concentration of the reactant to reduce to its $\frac{1}{32}$ level is $_______$ $\times 10^{-2}\min$. (Nearest integer)

(Given : $\ln 10=2.303$ and $\log 2=0.3010\text{)}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$K=20\min ^{-1}$

$\mathrm{t}_{1/2}=\frac{0.6932}{20}=\frac{\ln 2}{20}$

Required time $=\mathrm{n}\times \mathrm{t}_{1/2}$

$C=\frac{C_{0}}{2^{n}}=\frac{C_{0}}{32}$

$\Rightarrow$ $2^{n}=32$ = $2^{5}$

$\Rightarrow$ n = 5

$\begin{array}{ll} \text{Required time} & =\dfrac{5\times 0.6932}{20} \\  \\ =0.173\min  \\  \\ =17.3\times 10^{-2}\min  \end{array}$
